question.text: Mr. Karthik Iyer, a first-time LP, asks you about the scale of the Indian AIF industry today. Based on the current SEBI data referenced in Chapter 6, which of the following is the CORRECT approximate scale of cumulative commitments raised across all registered AIFs?

answer.text: Approximately INR 15.05 lakh crore as of September 30, 2025
Approximately INR 1.5 lakh crore as of September 30, 2025
Approximately INR 50 lakh crore as of September 30, 2025
Approximately INR 150 lakh crore as of September 30, 2025

explanation.text: The Logic: Section 6.5 of Chapter 6 states: 'Capital commitments raised by all registered AIFs (across categories) have surpassed INR 15.05 lakh crores as on September 30, 2025.' As on January 14, 2026, 1,750 AIFs were registered, up from just 21 in 2012. The Trap: Option A (INR 1.5 lakh crore) is off by 10x — tempting if the candidate misreads the decimal. Option D (INR 150 lakh crore) is 10x too large. Option B (INR 50 lakh crore) is fabricated to resemble a plausible 'big number'. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A/B Distributor exams also cite industry AUM milestones; XIX-C expects the Manager to anchor LP conversations in the correct current-market-size number. Manager's Pro-Tip: When discussing industry scale with LPs, pair the number with vintage trajectory — 21 funds in 2012 to 1,750 in 2026 and INR 15.05 lakh crore cumulative commitments — this contextualises why AIF is now a credible institutional-grade industry, not a niche product.
